correctness.rationale: The linear characters are Irr(G/G'), giving one principal and p^(2n)-1 nonprincipal characters of kernel index p. Standard extraspecial character theory gives p-1 nonlinear irreducibles of degree p^n indexed by nonprincipal center characters. Because the center has order p, those center characters are faithful; the nonlinear characters vanish off the center, so their kernels are trivial and their codegree is p^(n+1). The degree-squared sum closes the character count, and the packaged checker verifies both the formula and inverse reconstruction.

value.rationale: Extraspecial groups are a canonical infinite family with exactly two isomorphism types at each order, making them a natural stress test for the pseudo-algebra. The theorem gives a complete formula and a sharp information boundary: prime, symplectic rank, and order are recovered, while extraspecial type is systematically forgotten. This directly complements the literature's global negative result on order recovery.
